title: MZ Of Mice and Mascots Ch1

posts.author: MarioLuigi34
posts.body:
Hey guys, it's me; the creep who asked for free plugins that one time!
I've released the first chapter of my game "Of Mice and Mascots!" The development of future chapters is still being worked on, so I'm posting this here!
This game is a simple and easy first-person adventure game using MZ3D. Solve puzzles, shoot a gun, and walk from room to room interacting with objects for fun text! Characters are 2D cutout sprites, the world is bright and colorful yet dark and twisted underneath... you can... uh... press buttons to move... uh... okay...
"Chapter 1:
Mike Mouse awakes to find himself in an unfamiliar dark and damp place... his head pounding, his heart racing, and his soul broken, he must travel west to find what he's lost. Simple puzzles and an in-depth story pave Mike's path to salvation. This game is exactly what you expect of it; just another mascot horror game."
Link:

Thank you!

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I played your demo. I ended up stopping after the elevator crash, so I'm not sure how close to the end of the demo was but I think I got a good feel for what you're going for. You have some twists that I assume you want kept secret, so I'll be sticking any comments involving those in extra spoilers.
Spoiler:
Feedback
Going for a 3D game in RPG Maker is difficult, even with plugins it can feel pretty clunky, so I applaud you for attempting it. I do think you need to rework some of the art to work better with the 3D, objects like the hands that point which way to go can be completely invisible to the player depending on how they approach, so I often got stuck on an 'invisible' tile and couldn't tell if it was a mistake with the game or with me. To a similar point, the flat blocks that turn to face the character look odd when I'm looking at them from an angle, since it looks like I can go between them even if I can't. Finding a way to have those be solid and not turn would help make them feel more grounded in the maps.
Spoiler
The cameras around the starting areas before the twist are also hard to recognize due to the 3D plugin, maybe have those be simpler.
And since I'm touching on the graphics, I think you should adjust the height of the human sprites. I get that you want Mike to feel small compared to them, but right now he's crotch-height and it's hard to take any conversations seriously when Mike's just staring at someone's pants. Having him be more chest-height or having the camera pan up automatically during dialogue would help that a lot.
I also had some issues with the controls. When you have unique controls it's nice to have a tutorial book or a page in the menu where players can double-check what buttons do what. A lot of players will take a break and then come back to the game, and if they forget how to turn in place then they'll end up stuck with the option of either restarting to see the controls again or just fully quitting the game. If you include a list of controls that are easy to reach, then players won't have to worry about forgetting something. Controlling the camera with the mouse was also a challenge for me, I prefer to stick with keyboard-only but I was switching between the game and my notes, so when I clicked on the game with my mouse to bring it back into focus the camera would flail wildly until I stopped it by opening the menu. I didn't find a way to reset the camera fully, so I had to try and realign it with the mouse and that would leave it slightly off-center which messed with my sense of movement and made me miss some scares since I was looking too much at the floor.
Spoiler
I didn't seen the blue skeletal guy at first because I had messed up my camera, so it was a surprise when I turned around and it was there. But the fear from it quickly dissipated since it didn't actually cause any damage even though it played SEs and flashed the screen red. I do like the twist of it all being a movie so there isn't actually any danger, but I think from a player standpoint you need to treat that blue guy as a deadly enemy. Otherwise players may think later than enemies can't cause damage, or think you made a mistake when eventing the blue guy. And story-wise, it would make sense for a 'game over' (the director calling cut) in that situation if Mike is failing to avoid the blue guy and kept getting hit since it shouldn't happen then in the movie.
The room itself with the blue guy was a major jump in difficulty, since all the fences are hard to navigate around with a box. If the blue guy did do damage, it's possible that your players would give up there because they can't make it through the room in time. Limiting the number of turns required would still help teach your players how to maneuver blocks around obstacles without making it frustrating when they're trying to also avoid the blue guy.
There were a couple of other things that seemed odd:
Why an asterisk at the start of sentences? If it's a style choice, it looks odd alongside the quotation marks
There are a number of small spelling mistakes, so double-check all your messages to polish it up
After getting through the blue guy's room, Mike is started facing a wall
Add a visual element when the elevator is finished moving, right now it's impossible to tell with the sound off
Overall, you have a clear idea of what you want and deliver on it pretty well, but I think you need to tweak the controls and 3D elements to better support the story and gameplay.
Good luck with your project!

posts.author: MarioLuigi34
posts.body:
Thank you for giving my game a try!
The controls are something I can look into fixing up while I work on the second chapter. (I'm working on each chapter between standalone games, so I'll hopefully think of something by then!)
EDIT: I completely missed the point you were making about the 3D graphics my first time reading, disregarding what I said before, I'll add that to my list of stuff to work on.
EDIT 2: I forgot to mention, but in the credits for chapter one I say I have a new method for spellchecking that goes into effect for any future projects.
Also, it's the full first chapter. I posted it here as the game itself is unfinished.
If you finish the first chapter, let me know!

posts.author: MarioLuigi34
posts.body:
What I have for my fix right now:
- Making tutorial text clearer in that the game is controlled mostly with WASD and Mouse like a normal FPS.
- Adjusting height issue.
- Having tiles under sprites that can be invisible from certain directions to help with player confusion.
- Looking over in-game text.
- Making tutorials more clear.
- Adding Player Controls as a Key item.
- Changing the later puzzles for simplicity.
The new build should be up by the end of the week, mostly text and player clarity that are making it take so long.

- Made Level design more clear.
